To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

parental occupational exposure pre conception or both before and after conception to allergens or reactive chemical was associated with increased risk of asthma in their offspring, but only for asthma onset at 0 3 years.
parental occupational exposure to micro-organisms, pesticides, reactive chemicals and allergens pre conception or both before and after conception was not related with offspring asthma.
maternal exposure both pre conception and during pregnancy to allergens and to reactive chemicals was associated, respectively, with increased odds of early onset asthma in their children.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possible impact of parental occupational exposures on asthma in their offspring and whether the timing and duration of exposure is important.
the effects of parental occupational exposure on asthma development in their offspring.
the effects of parental occupational exposure on the development of asthma in the offspring.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence for an association between parental occupational exposures before conception or during pre and/or post conception, and offspring asthma.

the current evidence is not conclusive on the effects of parental occupational exposure on offspring respiratory health, but the current study did not find an effect of parental occupational exposure before conception.
parental occupational exposure pre and during pregnancy is not related to offspring respiratory health.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
parental occupational exposure before conception is not a risk factor for offspring asthma.
the association between parental exposure to allergens and chemicals and asthma in the offspring is not clear cut.
parental occupational exposure pre and during post conception is not associated with offspring asthma in the general population.
The main takeaway from our work is that
parental pre conception occupational exposure to micro-organisms and pesticides, as assessed by a job exposure matrix, does not appear to be related to asthma in offspring.

the association between parental pre conception occupational exposure and offspring respiratory health is complex and may be modified by the timing of exposure, the type of occupational exposures, and the age at asthma diagnosis.
we found no evidence of a link between parental occupational exposure pre and or post conception with asthma in their offspring.
